section: International climate initiatives - UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol, CDM, Paris Agreement, key COP outcomes, IPCC assessment reports
subsections: Climate justice - G20 New Delhi and Voice of Global South summits
UNFCCC COP hosted by India - edition, declaration adopted

accepted.s: The G20 New Delhi Summit was held on:
accepted.x: The G20 New Delhi Summit was held on 9–10 September 2023.
accepted.tq: Use the precise date rather than a nearby international-meeting date.
accepted.sec: Climate justice - G20 New Delhi and Voice of Global South summits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was adopted at the G20 New Delhi Summit?
o: Delhi Ministerial Declaration on Climate Change and Sustainable Development
BRICS Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance
accepted.x: The G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration adopted a Green Development Pact.
accepted.tq: Match the declaration or pact with the correct summit.
accepted.sec: Climate justice - G20 New Delhi and Voice of Global South summits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched at the:
o: BRICS Summit at Rio de Janeiro
accepted.x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched at the G20 New Delhi Summit in September 2023.
accepted.tq: Identify the forum associated with the launch of an initiative.
accepted.sec: Climate justice - G20 New Delhi and Voice of Global South summits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Voice of Global South Summits:
1. The summits were hosted by India from January 2023.
2. India has used the platform to argue for the finance and technology needs of developing countries.
3. The summits were established as a mechanism of the European Union's CBAM.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The summits were hosted by India from January 2023 and addressed developing-country finance and technology needs. They were not established as a CBAM mechanism.
accepted.tq: Reject the unrelated institutional claim and retain the two linked policy statements.
accepted.sec: Climate justice - G20 New Delhi and Voice of Global South summits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Mission LiFE, associated with India's climate contribution, primarily seeks to promote:
accepted.x: Mission LiFE is India's idea-level contribution centred on individual behaviour change.
accepted.tq: Infer the central objective from the nature of the mission rather than its launch venue.
accepted.sec: Climate justice - G20 New Delhi and Voice of Global South summits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the chronology of Mission LiFE?
o: Announced at COP26 and launched in October 2022
Announced at COP21 and launched in September 2023
Announced at COP27 and launched in November 2022
Announced at COP28 and launched in October 2023
accepted.x: Mission LiFE was announced at COP26 and launched in October 2022.
accepted.tq: Separate the announcement year and the launch year before selecting the sequence.
accepted.sec: Climate justice - G20 New Delhi and Voice of Global South summits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The BRICS Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance was associated with which of the following?
accepted.x: The declaration was associated with the BRICS meeting at Rio in July 2025 and supported Global South demands.
accepted.tq: Match the declaration with its city and date.
accepted.sec: Climate justice - G20 New Delhi and Voice of Global South summits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: COP8 was held in New Delhi in 2002 and adopted the:
o: Delhi Ministerial Declaration on Climate Change and Sustainable Development
BRICS Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance
accepted.x: COP8, held in New Delhi in 2002, adopted the Delhi Ministerial Declaration on Climate Change and Sustainable Development.
accepted.tq: Link the COP edition, host city and outcome in one factual recall question.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC COP hosted by India - edition, declaration adopted  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to India's proposal to host COP33, consider the following statements:
1. India withdrew its bid in April 2026.
2. The withdrawal followed a review of its commitments for 2028.
3. The withdrawal letter was dated 2 April 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India withdrew its bid in April 2026 after reviewing its 2028 commitments, and the withdrawal letter was dated 2 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Verify the event, its stated reason and the exact date together.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC COP hosted by India - edition, declaration adopted  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who had offered to host COP33 at COP28 in Dubai in 2023?
o: The Secretary-General of the United Nations
accepted.x: India's Prime Minister had offered to host COP33 at COP28 in Dubai in 2023.
accepted.tq: Identify the office-holder associated with the offer rather than the later host-country decision.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC COP hosted by India - edition, declaration adopted  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (COP)
a. COP21
b. COP26
c. COP27
d. COP29

List-II (Outcome)
i. New Collective Quantified Goal on Climate Finance
 ii. Paris Agreement
 iii. Glasgow Climate Pact
 iv. Loss and Damage Fund

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: COP21 adopted the Paris Agreement, COP26 produced the Glasgow Climate Pact, COP27 established the Loss and Damage Fund, and COP29 is associated with the New Collective Quantified Goal on Climate Finance.
accepted.tq: Start from the well-known COP21–Paris pair and resolve the remaining outcomes.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC COP hosted by India - edition, declaration adopted  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: COP30 is distinguished by which of the following features?
o: It was the first COP held in Paris.
It adopted the Delhi Ministerial Declaration.
It was the first COP held in the Amazon at Belém.
accepted.x: COP30 was the first COP held in the Amazon, at Belém.
accepted.tq: Use a first-of-its-kind geographical distinction.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC COP hosted by India - edition, declaration adopted  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
At Bonn SB64, the COP31 presidency, Türkiye, set which of the following 2035 goals?
1. A 35% share of electricity in final energy.
2. Halving the growth of global waste.
3. A 25% reduction in building energy intensity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The three stated 2035 goals were a 35% electricity share in final energy, halving the growth of global waste, and reducing building energy intensity by 25%.
accepted.tq: Retain all three specific numerical targets; none is an unrelated distractor.

accepted.s: According to the Indicators of Global Climate Change 2025 report, marine heatwaves:
o: Increased by 61% and were the fastest-worsening indicator
Remained unchanged and were not assessed
Declined by 61% and became the least-worsening indicator
Increased by 25% and became the second-fastest indicator
accepted.x: The report found that marine heatwaves had increased by 61% and were the fastest-worsening indicator.
accepted.tq: Check both the direction and the percentage instead of accepting a reversed trend.

accepted.s: Why are the consensus procedures of the CMP and CMA criticised by some observers?
o: Only developed countries may participate in them.
They operate without any parties or governments.
Consensus gives every party an effective veto.
accepted.x: Because the CMP and CMA work by consensus, every party can effectively block agreement, leading to the criticism that they resemble 'hop-on, hop-off buses'.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional consequence of consensus decision-making.

accepted.s: The criticism that the European Union's CBAM sidesteps UNFCCC principles has been particularly expressed by:
accepted.x: BRICS has viewed the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism as sidestepping UNFCCC principles.
accepted.tq: Match the criticism with the group that expressed it.

accepted.s: Persons displaced by sea-level rise are, as a category, outside the scope of the:
accepted.x: Climate refugees displaced by sea-level rise fall outside the legal scope of the 1951 Refugee Convention.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a climate-migration issue from the climate treaties themselves.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the first legally binding climate treaty?
accepted.x: The Kyoto Protocol was the first legally binding climate treaty.
accepted.tq: Use the FIRST clue to distinguish the earlier binding instrument from later agreements.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the criticism concerning the Green Climate Fund and Nepal?
o: The GCF was criticised for a seven-year delay on Nepal's GLOF proposal.
The GCF rejected all proposals concerning glacial lakes immediately.
The GCF transferred the proposal to the Kyoto Protocol.
Nepal delayed the GCF's establishment by seven years.
accepted.x: The Green Climate Fund was criticised for a seven-year delay in dealing with Nepal's proposal concerning a glacial lake outburst flood.
accepted.tq: Keep the actor, duration and proposal subject in the correct combination.

accepted.s: Nepal's request for Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage assistance after the August 2026 glacial-collapse flood was described as:
o: An early test of the fund
A challenge to the 1951 Refugee Convention
A review of the Paris Agreement's temperature goal
The first activation of the Kyoto Protocol
accepted.x: Nepal's request after the August 2026 glacial-collapse flood was viewed as an early test of the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage.
accepted.tq: Connect the disaster event with the institutional function being tested.

accepted.s: The unmet climate-finance promise of 100 billion dollars has primarily:
o: Made the Kyoto Protocol legally void
Ended the operation of the UNFCCC
accepted.x: Failure to meet the 100-billion-dollar promise has contributed to erosion of trust in climate negotiations.
accepted.tq: Link the financial shortfall with its stated political consequence.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the scientific basis of UNFCCC and COP negotiations:
1. The agreed scientific baseline supports UNFCCC and COP negotiations.
2. The Paris 1.5°C goal and net-zero-by-2050 benchmarks rest on SR1.5 and AR6.
3. SR1.5 and AR6 are unrelated to climate-policy benchmarks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The agreed scientific baseline informs negotiations, and the 1.5°C and net-zero-by-2050 benchmarks rest on SR1.5 and AR6. Statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed relationship in the third statement.

accepted.s: According to the WMO State of the Global Climate 2025 information, the atmospheric CO2 concentration in 2024 was:
accepted.x: The reported CO2 concentration for 2024 was 423.9 ppm.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely spaced numerical options by retaining the exact figure.

accepted.s: The oceans absorbed approximately how much additional heat in 2025?
accepted.x: The oceans absorbed an additional 23 zettajoules (ZJ) of heat in 2025.
accepted.tq: Watch the order of magnitude and the decimal-place trap.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about attribution of extreme weather events:
1. Single-event attribution of every extreme weather event to climate change is questioned.
2. AR6 notes that some local phenomena are difficult to attribute.
3. Attribution of all local phenomena is considered scientifically certain.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Single-event attribution is debated, and AR6 notes difficulty in attributing some local phenomena. The claim that all local phenomena are certain to attribute is false.
accepted.tq: Find the absolute word in the false statement and compare it with the cautious scientific position.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: International Solar Alliance — COP21, 2015 — France and India
Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure — COP21, 2015 — France and India
Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure — COP26 — Gurugram
accepted.x: The International Solar Alliance was established at COP21 in 2015 with France and India. CDRI was established in 2019 in New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Start with the institution's founding event and eliminate swapped dates and locations.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the International Solar Alliance is correct?
o: It is headquartered in Paris and was created at COP26.
Its headquarters are at New Delhi, and it was created in 2019.
Its headquarters are at Gurugram, making it the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.
It is a BRICS institution headquartered in Rio de Janeiro.
accepted.x: The International Solar Alliance is headquartered in Gurugram and is the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.
accepted.tq: Separate the headquarters fact from the similar CDRI location and date.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's position on its net-zero target for 2070?
o: India rejects CBDR and treats the target as an immediate obligation by 2030.
India bases the target exclusively on the 1951 Refugee Convention.
India has abandoned the target because of the CBAM.
India defends the target on the grounds of CBDR and development, although it is criticised as late.
accepted.x: India's 2070 net-zero target is criticised as late, while India defends it using the principles of common but differentiated responsibilities and development needs.
accepted.tq: Contrast criticism of the timeline with India's stated justification.

accepted.s: During India's chairship, BRICS rejected the:
o: European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism
Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
accepted.x: BRICS rejected the European Union's CBAM during India's chairship.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy instrument rather than a climate fund or treaty goal.
